security.lockDescription: Ask for a password before this terminal can be used on this device.
security.biometricUnlockDescription: Open the lock screen with this device's own unlock (Face ID, Touch ID, a fingerprint, Windows Hello) instead of typing the password.
security.biometricUnlockScreenOnly: Your password still works, and it stays the only way back in if the sensor stops recognising you.
security.biometricUnlockVaultNote: This opens the screen only. Your stored keys still ask for their own password. Add a passkey to your vault below to open both with one gesture.
security.biometricUnlockCoveredByVault: Your vault already unlocks with a passkey or Touch ID, and that opens the lock screen too. A second one here would do less.
security.turnOffDescription: Enter your current password to remove the lock from this device.
security.noRecoveryWarning: There is no password recovery. If you forget it, the only way back in erases this device's data. Save it in your password manager now.
security.triggersDescription: Choose the moments the password prompt should appear.
security.triggerStartupHint: Ask for the password on a cold start.
security.triggerIdleHint: Lock after {{minutes}} minutes with no mouse or keyboard.
security.triggerPeriodicHint: Lock again after a fixed time, however busy the session is.
security.triggerWakeHint: Lock when the machine comes back from sleep.
security.triggerTradeHint: Confirm an order you place by hand or through the assistant, including auto-approved proposals. Bots are never asked.
security.protectsBody: It puts a full-screen password prompt in front of the terminal, so someone at your desk cannot click around your positions, read your balances, or place an order. It encrypts nothing: your exchange API keys and wallet keys stay exactly where they were, and anyone with your unlocked computer and some technical skill can read this app’s local data without ever seeing the prompt.
security.protectsBots: Armed bots keep trading while the terminal is locked. Locking the screen is not pausing your strategies.
security.protectsDesktop: Your password check is stored in the system keychain and never leaves this computer.
security.protectsBrowser: This build stores the password check in browser storage. Clearing site data removes the lock. The desktop app is the supported home for this.
security.lockNowDescription: Close settings and lock the terminal immediately.
security.resetConfirmBody: This erases every exchange API key, wallet key, workspace, chart layout and chat on this computer. There is no undo and no password recovery. If you are signed in, settings that sync to the cloud come back when you sign in again. API keys and wallet keys never do, because they are only ever stored here.
security.vaultDescription: Encrypt your exchange API keys and wallet keys with a password or a passkey.
security.vaultAlsoUnlocks: Any of these also unlocks the terminal lock screen: one password serves both.
security.biometricNeedsVault: Set up the vault with a password first. Touch ID is then added on top.
security.vaultRemoveLastBlocked: This is the only way into your vault. Add another before removing it.
security.vaultRemoveBiometricOnlyBlocked: Touch ID cannot be the only way in: the fingerprints on this Mac can change. Keep a password or a passkey.
security.vaultProtectsBody: With a vault, your API keys and wallet keys are stored encrypted. Someone who copies this browser profile (or this device's storage) gets ciphertext they cannot open without your password or your passkey.
security.vaultCeiling: It does not protect keys while you are using them. Anything running inside this page can ask the unlocked vault for a key, the same way the app does. The desktop app remains the recommendation for your most valuable keys.
security.vaultNoRecovery: There is no recovery. Lose every way in and the encrypted keys are gone: the only way back into the app erases this device's data.
security.vaultDesktopToggleHint: Your keys are already in the system keychain. Turn this on to add a password or a passkey on top.
security.vaultDesktopOptOutBody: Your keys go back to being protected by the system keychain alone. Nothing is deleted, and you can turn the vault back on later.
security.vaultMigrated_one: Moved 1 key you already had into the vault.
security.vaultMigrated_other: Moved {{count}} keys you already had into the vault.
security.vaultMigrationFailed: Vault setup did not finish. Your keys are still readable. Open the vault to complete it.
security.vaultSharedBackoff: The vault and the lock screen share one attempt limit, so too many wrong passwords delays both.
security.vaultCliNote: The command-line tool takes API keys as arguments and never reads the vault.
security.hardLockDescription: Lock the vault, not just the screen.
security.hardLockWarning: Locks the vault, not just the screen. Live bots and automations stop trading until you unlock. Paper bots keep running.
security.hardLockConfirmBody: Live bots and automations stop trading until you unlock again. Paper bots keep running.

botsPage.localBody: Your strategies execute here, in Pairlens, rather than on a server we operate. That is what keeps your keys and your logic yours. The tradeoff is real: quit Pairlens or let this computer sleep and your bots stop with it, and an open position is left unwatched until you come back.

localOnly.badgeAria: Learn how your keys are kept private
localOnly.title: Your keys never leave this device
localOnly.subtitle: Exactly what happens to the API keys and wallet keys you add, including what this cannot protect.
localOnly.statusDesktop: Right now: your keys sit in {{vault}}, on this computer only.
localOnly.statusDesktopVault: Right now: {{vault}}, with your own vault encrypting every key on top.
localOnly.statusBrowserVault: Right now: every key encrypted in your vault, in this browser only.
localOnly.statusBrowserNone: No vault on this browser yet. You will set one up before the first key can be saved.
localOnly.deviceBody: Your exchange API keys and wallet keys are saved on this computer and nowhere else. They are never uploaded to Pairlens: not when you sign in, not when your settings sync, not when the assistant reads a chart. There is no copy on our servers to leak.
localOnly.osBodyDesktop: They live in {{vault}}, the same protected store your system uses for its own passwords, encrypted on disk and handed out only to this app.
localOnly.osBodyDesktopVault: They live in {{vault}}, the same protected store your system uses for its own passwords. Your vault adds a layer on top: every value is sealed with AES-256-GCM before the keychain ever sees it.
localOnly.osBodyBrowser: Every value is sealed with AES-256-GCM before it touches browser storage. One data key encrypts them all, and that key is never written down in the clear.
localOnly.unlockBody: A password, stretched with 600,000 rounds of PBKDF2-SHA256; a passkey on your phone or security key; or Touch ID. Each one wraps the same data key, so you can keep more than one way in. Pairlens never receives any of them.
localOnly.openSourceTitle: Public source code, verify it yourself
localOnly.openSourceBody: Pairlens's code is public. You, a developer friend, or even an AI can read it and confirm your keys really do stay put.
localOnly.limitsRunning: While the app is open and unlocked it can read your keys. That is how it places your orders. The encryption defends a copied disk or browser profile, not a machine someone is already sitting at.
localOnly.limitsNoRecovery: There is no recovery. Lose every way in and the encrypted keys are gone for good.

ai-research-desk.tagline: A chart flanked by the symbol wire and the global feed.
ai-research-desk.description: Pair a chart with both the symbol news feed and the global wire, for catalyst-driven trading where the story matters as much as the tape. The AI assistant rides in the dock, so it is on hand here without taking a column.

chart-analysis.name: Chart Analysis
chart-analysis.tagline: Chart and data left, execution right.
chart-analysis.description: A study-oriented split: chart, data, and risk on the left; the order book and trade ticket on the right.

chart-focus.name: Chart Focus
chart-focus.tagline: One big chart with tabbed data underneath.
chart-focus.description: A single-column layout that gives the chart maximum room, with positions, the data log, and the trade ticket tucked into a tab strip below.

classic-terminal.name: Spot Execution
classic-terminal.tagline: Best bid and ask across every venue you connected.
classic-terminal.description: The default spot layout: chart with the tape and positions below it, and a rail that leads with the cross-venue ladder above the book and ticket.

command-center.name: 4K Command Center
command-center.tagline: The full command center for a 4K display.
command-center.description: Everything on screen for a 4K monitor: order book and pair info, chart with the risk bar, positions and social, and a trade ticket rail.

cross-venue-desk.name: Cross-Venue Desk
cross-venue-desk.tagline: One pair, every venue, cheapest fill on top.
cross-venue-desk.description: Built around the Multi-Price panel: the active pair quoted on every venue that lists it, ranked by price so the best fill is the top row. A chart and the tape sit beside it, with the order book and a trade ticket ready to act on the gap.

day-trader-pro.name: Day Trader Pro
day-trader-pro.tagline: Scan, chart, and trade the intraday session.
day-trader-pro.description: A balanced three-column desk: a markets scanner on the left, a large chart in the middle, and an order book plus trade ticket and open positions on the right. The everyday driver for active crypto trading.

dex-degen.name: DEX Degen
dex-degen.tagline: On-chain charts, swaps, and the social feed.
dex-degen.description: Built for on-chain hunting: a chart with a swap ticket, recent tickers to catch new listings, and the social feed for alpha. Route swaps through a DEX connector such as Jupiter.

dex-terminal.name: DEX Terminal
dex-terminal.tagline: On-chain trading without the fake order book.
dex-terminal.description: The default on-chain layout: a chart over pool stats, the on-chain tape beside it, and a swap ticket above the aggregator route so slippage has a stated cause. There is no order book column: pool-quoted depth is synthetic, so it is not shown.

dual-charts.name: Dual Charts
dual-charts.description: Two independent chart panes side by side. Each keeps its own market, timeframe, and chart type. Set a different pair per pane with its pair picker.

equities-desk.name: Equities Desk
equities-desk.tagline: Trade stocks with a scanner, chart, and positions.
equities-desk.description: A stock-trading layout: the markets scanner, a chart, open positions, and the news wire. Connect the Alpaca broker plugin to stream US equities and route orders.

equities-terminal.name: Equities Terminal
equities-terminal.tagline: The session clock over the chart, Level 1 over the ticket.
equities-terminal.description: The default stock layout: the session clock leads, then the chart with time and sales and positions below it, and a rail carrying Level 1 quotes over the ticket and the symbol wire. Outside regular hours the clock says so, and the ticket goes limit-only.

home-pulse.name: Spot Discovery
home-pulse.tagline: Open on what moved, and why.
home-pulse.description: The spot home board: a market pulse strip over the movers table and the sector tape, with the full scanner beside it and news over your watchlist. Everything on it works without an account.

laptop-focus.name: Laptop Focus
laptop-focus.tagline: Vertical single-column layout tuned for laptops.
laptop-focus.description: A compact, vertical layout that fits a laptop screen: chart on top, a data tab strip, and a slim risk bar.

laptop-split.name: Laptop Split
laptop-split.tagline: Chart and data left, the ticket right, sized for laptops.
laptop-split.description: A two-column split sized for laptops: chart, positions, and risk on the left, with the trade ticket on the right.

market-discovery.name: Market Discovery
market-discovery.tagline: Find what is moving before you commit.
market-discovery.description: A pure discovery board: the markets scanner, top movers, a sector heatmap, your watchlist, and the Fear & Greed gauge. No chart, no ticket. Just for hunting the next setup.

markets-board.name: Markets Board
markets-board.description: The full-width markets scanner, the simplest way to browse and sort every tradable pair.

markets-overview.name: Markets Overview
markets-overview.tagline: Scanner beside your movers and watchlist.
markets-overview.description: The markets scanner alongside the top movers and your watchlist, a balanced home for finding and tracking setups.

news-board.name: News Board
news-board.tagline: Markets alongside movers and the news feed.
news-board.description: The markets scanner beside the top movers and the live news feed, a home base for catalyst-driven trading.

perps-terminal.name: Perps Terminal
perps-terminal.tagline: The futures desk: positions with mark and liquidation.
perps-terminal.description: The default perpetual-futures layout: a large chart with the tape, open contracts (entry, mark, liquidation), and market data tabbed below it, with an order book over a leverage-aware ticket on the right.

portfolio-command.name: Portfolio Command
portfolio-command.tagline: Balances, positions, and risk at a glance.
portfolio-command.description: An account-centric cockpit: your portfolio breakdown, open positions, live risk guardrails, and a watchlist to keep an eye on the rest of the book. For managing what you already hold.

prediction-terminal.name: Prediction Terminal
prediction-terminal.tagline: The question first, then the odds.
prediction-terminal.description: The default prediction-market layout: the event header over a probability chart, with the headlines that moved it below, the book and a ticket that states max payout and max loss before you stake, and the neighbouring outcomes on the right.

prediction-discovery.name: Prediction Discovery
prediction-discovery.tagline: Browse live event markets, not a catalog of pairs.
prediction-discovery.description: A home board built for event contracts: a category rail beside the event board, with the biggest odds moves over the contracts closest to settling. Install a prediction venue such as Kalshi or Polymarket to fill it.

quad-charts.name: Quad Charts
quad-charts.description: Four independent charts in a 2×2 grid, a full multi-chart cockpit for tracking several markets at once.

quant-signals.name: Quant Signals
quant-signals.tagline: Data log, heatmap, and risk for signal-driven trading.
quant-signals.description: A data-first desk: a chart paired with the raw data log, a liquidity heatmap, live risk state, and the markets scanner. For traders who read the tape as numbers, not candles.

scalpers-cockpit.name: Scalper's Cockpit
scalpers-cockpit.tagline: Chart, book, and one-click entry. Nothing else.
scalpers-cockpit.description: A minimal two-column cockpit for fast execution: a chart beside a live order book, market depth, and a trade-entry ticket. Built for speed on a single screen.

sector-analysis.name: Sector Analysis
sector-analysis.description: A discovery board with a sector heatmap in the middle: scanner on the left, heatmap in the center, and movers over your watchlist on the right.

swing-overview.name: Swing Overview
swing-overview.tagline: Trend context with a watchlist and the movers.
swing-overview.description: A calmer layout for multi-day positions: a full chart alongside your watchlist, the top movers, and pair fundamentals. Enough context to size a swing without the noise of an execution desk.

trading.name: Trading
trading.tagline: Order book and ticket beside a full-height chart.
trading.description: A two-column execution desk: order book over the trade ticket on the left, and the chart with positions and risk taking the rest of the width.

triple-charts.name: Triple Charts
triple-charts.tagline: One large chart with two stacked beside it.
triple-charts.description: A large primary chart with two smaller charts stacked to the right, each independent, for watching a lead pair against two others.

ultrawide-dashboard.name: Ultrawide Dashboard
ultrawide-dashboard.tagline: Every panel spread across an ultrawide monitor.
ultrawide-dashboard.description: A four-column dashboard for ultrawide displays: order book, chart with risk, positions and the data log, and a trade ticket rail.

ultrawide-trading.name: Ultrawide Trading
ultrawide-trading.tagline: Order book, depth, chart, and execution across the width.
ultrawide-trading.description: An ultrawide execution layout: order book and market depth on the left, chart with positions in the center, and the trade ticket on the right.

ultrawide-trading-floor.name: Ultrawide Trading Floor
ultrawide-trading-floor.tagline: Everything, everywhere. For the big screen.
ultrawide-trading-floor.description: A four-column command center that fills an ultrawide or second monitor: scanner, chart, order book and depth, and a trade ticket over your open positions. The maximalist layout.

perps-discovery.name: Perps Discovery
perps-discovery.tagline: Scan by cost of carry, not by price.
perps-discovery.description: The futures home board: the funding matrix over the basis monitor, with open interest and the funding extremes beside them. It ranks perps by what holding them costs, which is the question a price scanner never answers.

dex-discovery.name: DEX Discovery
dex-discovery.tagline: Pick the chain, then the pool.
dex-discovery.description: The on-chain home board: a chain rail with gas and liquidity, pools ranked by volume against liquidity over the flow chart, and the selected pool on the right, one click from its chart and a swap. Chains you have no connector for never appear.

equities-discovery.name: Equities Discovery
equities-discovery.tagline: The trading day, by the calendar that runs it.
equities-discovery.description: The stock home board: where the session is right now, who reports and when, and the macro releases due, with the movers and the news wire beside them. The clock comes from the broker calendar, so holidays and half days are right.

spot-research.name: Spot Research
spot-research.description: For positions held longer than a session: chart over the pair dossier, the pair's own news wire beside it, and a quote-sized ticket over its sector peers. No order book, so no depth stream opens.

perps-carry.name: Perps Carry
perps-carry.tagline: What the next funding stamp costs you.
perps-carry.description: For a perp you intend to hold: the funding belt above the chart with the countdown, the current and predicted rate and what your size pays or earns, open contracts below, and the book over a leverage-aware ticket.

perps-risk.name: Perps Risk
perps-risk.tagline: Where the position dies, and the limits that stop it.
perps-risk.description: The same pair read as exposure: the chart over a liquidation map, margin health above your guardrails, and the ticket on the right. The limits are editable in place, so a size cap is adjusted where the trade happens rather than in Settings.

dex-liquidity.name: DEX Liquidity
dex-liquidity.tagline: Your range, your fees, your impermanent loss.
dex-liquidity.description: The LP side of a pool: the chart with your range on it, fees accrued and the APR they imply, time in range, and impermanent loss measured against simply holding. The range editor sits beside it, so a position is rebalanced without leaving the chart.

dex-cross-chain.name: DEX Cross-Chain
dex-cross-chain.tagline: The same token, every chain, gas included.
dex-cross-chain.description: A board for moving between chains: the chain ladder prices the token everywhere with gas folded into the total, the bridge route states its fee and how long it takes, and transfers still confirming sit beside them with their current stage.

equities-company.name: Equities Company
equities-company.description: For holding a stock rather than trading it: the chart over valuation, growth, margins, the next catalyst and the analyst range, with the symbol wire beside it and your position above the ticket.

prediction-race.name: Prediction Race
prediction-race.tagline: Every runner priced, and the overround stated.
prediction-race.description: For an event with a field rather than two sides: the header with the runner count and the overround, a stacked-shares chart, and a ladder that prices every runner and stakes from the row. The basket sums to the overround, so sweeping the field is visibly not free money.

prediction-crypto-updown.name: Crypto Up/Down
prediction-crypto-updown.tagline: Every open window, against the tape it settles on.
prediction-crypto-updown.description: The recurring crypto contracts on both venues in one table: Kalshi opens a fifteen-minute window on five assets, Polymarket an hourly and a daily one on four. Each row carries the settlement reference, live spot, the distance between them and what a driftless diffusion at recent realized volatility makes of the time remaining, so the odds have something to be compared against.

nft-terminal.name: NFT Desk
nft-terminal.tagline: A collection as a book, not a gallery.
nft-terminal.description: Floor chart over a two-sided ladder, with listings and collection offers as real depth. The sales tape, the items grid and trait floors share the tabs below.

nft-collector.name: Collector
nft-collector.tagline: Pick the token, not the floor.
nft-collector.description: The items grid at full width with trait floors beside it, for buying one specific token rather than whatever is cheapest.

nft-discovery.name: NFT Discovery
nft-discovery.tagline: What is moving across NFT markets.
nft-discovery.description: Collections ranked by volume with floor moves beside them, a chain filter, the market-wide overview, fresh mints and the whale tape.

nft-flow.name: NFT Flow
nft-flow.description: Whale sales across every indexed collection, with floor movers and the rankings table alongside.

memecoin-discovery.name: Memecoin Discovery
memecoin-discovery.tagline: Four columns, one for each stage of the curve.
memecoin-discovery.description: The launchpad board: minted in the last hour, climbing the bonding curve with progress against the graduation threshold, migrated to a real pool, and the large caps that outlived their cycle. Every row carries market cap, liquidity, and buys against sells, and clicking one opens its chart and a swap ticket.

memecoin-terminal.name: Memecoin Terminal
memecoin-terminal.tagline: Market cap, flow, and who can still mint.
memecoin-terminal.description: The default memecoin layout: a chart over the flow strip that puts buys against sells at four horizons, supply and holder count in the middle, the deployer audit under it, and a swap ticket on the right. No order book: a bonding curve does not have one.

memecoin-sniper.name: Memecoin Sniper
memecoin-sniper.tagline: The curve on the left, the ticket on the right.
memecoin-sniper.description: Built for working launches: new mints and the graduating ladder stay on screen while the chart, the flow strip and the swap ticket fill the rest. The safety panel sits under the ticket, because the mint authority is the last thing worth checking before an order.

cut-if-stalls.title: Cut it if it stalls
